sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Columbus
sections.html:
Columbus and Muscogee County are a single consolidated government, so one Tax Commissioner sends the bills and takes the payments for the whole city. The Muscogee County Board of Tax Assessors decides taxability and value. City Council appoints its members to fixed terms under state law.

City Council sets the mill rate for city operations. The school board recommends its own rate, which City Council must, with few exceptions, set for the schools. Georgia no longer has a state ad valorem tax, a change that took effect in 2016. The Board of Equalization is made up of Muscogee County citizens appointed by the grand jury, and the Clerk of Superior Court administers it.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collects, handles delinquent tax and tax sales.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: value, exemptions, appeals. The office help desk is 706-225-4398.
  • Board of Equalization: hears value, uniformity and exemption disputes.

The assessors' board meets Wednesdays at 9:00am in the City Services Building at 3111 Citizens Way.

Columbus sits on the Chattahoochee River across from Phenix City, Alabama, about 100 miles southwest of Atlanta. It is Georgia's second most populous city and the seat of Muscogee County. Fort Benning, south of the city, is a major source of buyers and renters.

The 2025 estimate is 202,171 residents, down 2.3% from the 2020 base. Owners live in just 50.8% of homes, and a typical owned home is valued at $193,900 against average rent of $1,106. That renter-heavy mix means many Columbus sellers are landlords, and for a rental the tax bill still follows the January 1 owner.

The Tax Commissioner organizes the year by month. Assessment notices go out in May, bills arrive in August, and payment begins in October.

Columbus property tax dates by month
MonthWhat happens
April 1Mobile home bills due; homestead deadline; business personal property, aircraft and watercraft returns due
MayAnnual notice of assessment mailed; appeals within 45 days of the notice date
JulyTaxing authorities advertise and set millage rates
AugustReal and personal property bills mailed
OctoberBills due: a 40% installment or payment in full
DecemberRemaining 60% due

A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during the appeal window. Use the exact payment dates printed on your bill.

The bill splits into a 40% installment in October and the remaining 60% in December, or you can pay the full amount in October. A sale that closes between those payments needs the title company to know how much has already been paid.

The person who owns the property on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax, no matter who owns the house later. Both buyer and seller may get a bill, and the office does not decide who pays what share. Closing documents divide it.

If the tax goes unpaid, the lien lands on the January 1 owner unless the seller supplies proof inside 90 days of the due date that the buyer took over the liability. A recorded deed in the new owner's name and closing language that clearly assigns the tax to the buyer both count as proof. Once it is verified, the lien may be recorded against the buyer.

The standard exemption is a $13,500 reduction in assessed value, and the Tax Commissioner adds age, military and surviving-spouse exemptions on top. You can apply at any time in the calendar year after the property becomes your primary residence, up to and including April 1 of the year you want the exemption.

  • Standard homestead (H1): $13,500 off assessed value, applying to the maintenance and operation levies of the county and school board, not bond debt.
  • Elderly general (H2): age 65 or older by January 1, with household net income not over $10,000 for the prior year, plus income documents.
  • Disabled veteran (H5): up to $121,812, with a VA benefits letter.
  • Unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in a war or armed conflict: up to $121,812, with Department of Defense documents.
  • Surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed or fatally injured in duty: 100% exemption.

You need a copy of the recorded deed and a Georgia driver's license showing your current address, and voter and vehicle registration must be in Muscogee County. After approval the exemption renews until you move, the ownership changes or you seek a different one. A property tax deferral exists for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, running until a change of ownership or until the deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
The Muscogee County Tax Commissioner can place a tax lien, called a fifa, and levy the property for a tax sale. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates, and a property that fails to sell at a tax sale goes back into rotation for later sales. The Delinquent Tax section includes a tax sale list and a class registration page for bidders.

Staff cannot give legal advice, and owners with a lien or levy are told to consult an attorney. For a seller, the practical sequence is simple: get the payoff from the Tax Commissioner, confirm it with the title company, and clear the lien from the sale proceeds if the house sells before a tax sale date. A cash sale suits this well, because the payoff and title work are the only steps between you and the closing table.

Personal property has its own rule. Taxable tangible personal property other than motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value, as determined by the assessors, does not exceed $20,000.

Appeals are due 45 days after the date on the notice of assessment, which goes out in May. The Board of Tax Assessors receives and reviews the appeal, and the Board of Equalization hears matters of value, uniformity, taxability and denied exemptions.

Real property appeals go to ccgboa@columbusga.org, and personal property appeals go to ppboa@columbusga.org. Questions about real property appeals can also go to 706-225-4398. A homeowner who has not yet claimed a homestead can file that application during the same appeal period instead of appealing.

Keep the notice itself. It states the value the county will use for the bill, and the 45 days run from the date printed on it.

faqs.q: When are Columbus property tax bills due?
faqs.a: In October, as either a 40% installment or payment in full, with the remaining 60% due in December. The exact day is printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for Columbus property tax after I sell?
faqs.a: The person who owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax. Closing documents normally divide it, and a lien moves to the buyer only with proof delivered within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: How much is the standard homestead exemption in Columbus?
faqs.a: It is a $13,500 reduction in assessed value. It applies to the county and school maintenance and operation levies, not the bond portion.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Columbus?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, which is mailed in May. A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during that window.

faqs.q: Does the Columbus Tax Commissioner sell tax liens?
faqs.a: No. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates. A property that does not sell at a tax sale returns to the rotation for future sales.
